business_problem: Würth IT wanted to reduce the time employees spent on routine communication and meeting follow-up tasks across the Würth Group so they could focus more on higher-value work.
solution_summary: Würth IT evaluated Copilot for Microsoft 365 as a digital assistant across the Würth Group’s existing Microsoft 365 cockpit. The rollout focused on routine knowledge-work flows already happening in Teams, Outlook, and Word: meeting transcripts are summarized into decisions and actions, bullet-point notes become well-structured multilingual emails, and presentation or document preparation starts from Copilot-generated drafts instead of blank pages. Because the assistant lives inside tools employees already use, Würth IT could identify role-based use cases quickly during the early access program and distribute test licenses across companies and locations without redesigning the collaboration stack. The implementation pattern is to feed Copilot the user’s meeting transcript or prompt context inside Microsoft 365, have it generate the first draft or summary, and let employees spend more time on higher-value work across sales, administration, and shared services.

solution_components.name: Copilot for Microsoft 365
solution_components.role: Generates meeting summaries, email drafts, and other productivity outputs inside the Microsoft 365 workflow.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Teams
solution_components.role: Provides meeting transcripts and collaboration context for Copilot summaries.

solution_components.name: Outlook
solution_components.role: Is the workspace where users turn bullet points into structured multilingual emails with Copilot assistance.

solution_components.name: Word
solution_components.role: Acts as one of the Microsoft 365 applications where Copilot-generated content is consumed.

data_flow: Meeting transcripts and user prompts from Microsoft 365 apps are passed to Copilot for Microsoft 365, which generates summaries and drafts that employees review and use inside Teams, Outlook, and Word.
business_outcome: Würth IT identified practical Copilot use cases quickly, improved efficiency for multilingual communication and meeting follow-up, and built confidence for wider adoption across the group.
architecture_clues: Test licenses were distributed across the group during the early access program
